raw_case_text:
A 42-year-old man from Chhapra, Bihar, visited the outpatient department of Rajendra Memorial Research Institute of Medical Sciences (RMRIMS), Indian Council of Medical Research, Patna, on December 10, 2018, with non-itching nodular eruptions on his face, hands, and abdomen. The patient had a history of VL 8 months back. On physical examination, the patient was afebrile and non-anemic, with no hepatosplenomegaly, and skin lesions with intact sensitivity. On investigation, his rK39 strip test was positive. Hence, PKDL was suspected,and the patient was advised to undergo skin smear microscopy and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) analysis. His skin smear report was positive for Leishman-donovan bodies, and the parasite load for qPCR was 6723 parasites/microg of DNA. Hence, the patient was diagnosed with PKDL. 
The patient was prescribed 100 mg of oral miltefosine capsules daily for 28 days. After 15 days of miltefosine consumption, he developed blurred vision, redness, photophobia, and foreign body sensation in both eyes (Figure 1). He stopped taking miltefosine on his own, but his symptoms did not improve. Six days later, he visited RMRIMS, Patna. The patient was referred to a higher ophthalmological center for consultation by a trained ophthalmologist. His ophthalmic investigation revealed best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in the right and left eyeof 6/9 and 6/18, respectively. There was ciliary congestion in both eyes with no mucopurulent discharge. Anterior chamber examination revealed cells and flares in the anterior chamber along with fine keratic precipitates over the endothelium in both eyes. There was dense senile arcus in both eyes and mild posterior subcapsular cataract in the left eye. Posterior segment examination revealed no macular edema on +90D examination in either eye. Optical coherence tomography was not performed as the +90D examination showed no macular edema. Indirect ophthalmoscopy examinations were normal in both eyes. Routine laboratory examinations, including total blood cell count, differential white blood cell count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, chest radiography, Mantoux test, venereal disease research laboratory test, and antinuclear antibody test were performed to exclude other common causes of uveitis. The results were insignificant to establish any systemic association for uveitis. Therefore, a presumptive diagnosis of acute anterior non-granulomatous uveitis was made, and the routine treatment for typical anterior uveitis was started. He was treated with topical antibiotics and steroid eye drops. After 3 weeks of treatment, his ophthalmological examination revealed resolution of the uveitis. BCVA was recorded as 6/6 and 6/12 in the right and left eye, respectively. No cells or flare was present in the anterior segment examination. Posterior segment examination was normal on +90D and indirect ophthalmoscopy examination. The patient was administered 30 mg/kg of liposomal amphotericin B (6 doses of 5 mg/kg twice weekly for 3 weeks) in 5% dextrose intravenously. Six months post-treatment, all the skin lesions disappeared and the qPCR report showed negligible parasites.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 42-year-old male with post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis presented with blurred vision, bilateral eye redness, photophobia, and foreign body sensation after starting miltefosine.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to RMRIMS with non-itching nodular skin eruptions on his face, hands, and abdomen 8 months after completing treatment for visceral leishmaniasis. He was diagnosed with post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL) and prescribed oral miltefosine capsules (100 mg daily for 28 days). After 15 days of miltefosine therapy, he developed acute blurred vision, bilateral ocular redness, photophobia, and foreign body sensation in both eyes. He self-discontinued miltefosine, but symptoms persisted, prompting referral to an ophthalmology center 6 days later.
subjective.past_medical_history: Visceral leishmaniasis treated 8 months prior. Origin: Chhapra, Bihar, India (endemic region).
subjective.review_of_systems: Bilateral ocular pain, redness, photophobia, foreign body sensation, blurred vision. Denies pruritus of skin lesions. Home medications: miltefosine 100 mg daily (discontinued). Allergies: None documented.

objective.physical_examination: General: afebrile, non-anemic, no hepatosplenomegaly. Dermatologic: non-itching nodular eruptions on the face, hands, and abdomen with intact tactile sensation. Ophthalmologic: best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) 6/9 in right eye and 6/18 in left eye; bilateral ciliary injection/congestion without mucopurulent discharge; anterior chamber revealed cells and flares with fine endothelial keratic precipitates in both eyes; bilateral dense senile arcus and mild posterior subcapsular cataract in left eye; posterior segment normal on +90D and indirect ophthalmoscopy (no macular edema).
objective.routine_investigations: Hematology and serology: total blood cell count, differential white blood cell count, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) normal/unremarkable. Chest radiography: normal. Infectious and autoimmune serologies: Mantoux tuberculin test, Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) test, and antinuclear antibody (ANA) test were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Skin smear microscopy and quantitative PCR (qPCR): performed on facial/abdominal nodular lesions.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL) complicated by miltefosine-induced acute anterior non-granulomatous uveitis.
Diagnostic confirmation: Positive rK39 strip test; slit-skin smear microscopy demonstrated Leishman-Donovan (LD) bodies; quantitative PCR (qPCR) demonstrated a parasite load of 6,723 parasites/microg of DNA.
Differentials ruled out: Lepromatous leprosy (intact sensation, no thickened nerves), ocular syphilis (negative VDRL), tuberculosis (negative Mantoux, normal chest X-ray), and autoimmune anterior uveitis (negative ANA).
Treatment and clinical course: Miltefosine was permanently withheld. Acute anterior uveitis was treated with topical antibiotics and corticosteroid eye drops, leading to complete resolution of uveitis within 3 weeks (BCVA improved to 6/6 OD and 6/12 OS; resolution of anterior chamber cells and flare). PKDL was subsequently treated with intravenous liposomal amphotericin B (30 mg/kg cumulative dose given as 6 infusions of 5 mg/kg twice weekly for 3 weeks in 5% dextrose). At 6 months post-treatment, all cutaneous lesions completely resolved and repeat qPCR demonstrated negligible parasite load.
